case_title: PAULMELI AND ANR. v. STATE OF TAMIL NADU TR. INSP. OF POLICE
aggravating_circumstances: Indiscriminate cuts caused over the victim's body using aruval resulting in his death
neutral_facts: The prosecution case revolves around an incident where 17 persons, including the appellants, unlawfully assembled with a common object to murder the victim. The victim was attacked with an aruval, resulting in his death. His two sons intervened and sustained injuries. The FIR was lodged promptly, and investigations were carried out. The trial court initially acquitted all the accused, but in a fresh trial, the trial court acquitted all the accused except the appellants, who were convicted under Section 302 of the IPC and sentenced to life imprisonment and a fine of Rs. 2000 each. The High Court upheld the order. The evidence includes medical reports detailing the injuries sustained by the victim and his sons, as well as witness statements supporting the prosecution's case. The accused were identified by the victim's wife, who was able to recognize them despite the darkness due to their close relationship. The medical evidence corroborates the injuries caused by the aruval, and the courts below found that the injuries could have been caused by the attack. The evidence of a hostile witness was considered, and relevant parts of the testimony were accepted. The courts emphasized the importance of separating grain from chaff in the evidence and noted that the maxim 'falsus in uno, falsus in omnibus' does not apply in India.
